claims.text: Entering an over-quantity on the new-loan Step 2 form blocks progress without a clear validation message. Evidence: "Change \"Units of Canon C70 Cinema Camera\" to 4" when the row says "3 of 3 available"; after clicking Continue to review, "The app stays on Step 2 and preserves the entered values, but it displays no error or explanation. The user cannot tell why \"Continue to review\" did nothing."
claims.rationale: Verified via curl that the clean server's schedule check returns the exact spec message ('Only 1 unit of Canon C70 Cinema Camera is available.'), so the silent block is a client-side gap (native constraint validation instead of the SPEC 1.6 inline message). No catalog fault touches step-2 quantity validation, so the behavior is shared with the clean build and violates SPEC 1.6/7.2.

claims.text: Over-quantity validation on the Units field gives only an unclear native browser error. Evidence: "Over-quantity validation gives unclear native Units error" (Severity: major). Restates the inadequate over-quantity validation feedback covered by C001.
claims.rationale: duplicate of C001

claims.text: Over-quantity validation shows a vague native message with no item or stock context. Evidence: "Over-quantity validation uses a vague native message that omits the item and stock rationale." (Severity: major). Restates the inadequate over-quantity validation feedback covered by C001.
claims.rationale: duplicate of C001

claims.text: In the equipment catalogue, the availability of the MacBook Pro 16-inch Edit Laptop is not visible without scrolling. Evidence: "Equipment catalogue requires scrolling to view MacBook Pro 16-inch Edit Laptop availability" (Severity: minor).
claims.rationale: Needing to scroll to see one catalogue row is viewport layout friction, not a SPEC violation; the availability data is present and correct.

claims.text: The quantity control for an item is only discoverable after the item has been added; none is offered beforehand. Evidence: "The Canon quantity path was only discoverable after adding the item; there was no quantity control before pressing Add item." (Severity: minor).
claims.rationale: SPEC 7.2 deliberately designs step 2 this way: items are added from the Add equipment list and the units box appears on the added row. The complaint is a discoverability preference, not a violation.

claims.text: Borrower-form validation messages persist after the offending fields are corrected, leaving stale errors on screen. Evidence: "Corrected borrower fields keep stale validation messages, making the form state hard to trust." (Severity: minor).
claims.rationale: SPEC 1.6 ties message clearing to the next form check, and the clean server verifiably clears corrected fields on recheck (curl: refusal responses list only currently-failing fields). A message persisting until resubmission matches the SPEC, and the claim gives no evidence messages survived a resubmit.

claims.text: Borrower validation errors do not clear after valid corrections. Evidence: "Borrower validation errors remain after valid field corrections" (Severity: minor). Restates the stale borrower validation messages covered by C006.
claims.rationale: duplicate of C006

claims.text: Accessibility scanning reports widespread color-contrast violations affecting readability of text across the app. Evidence: "Accessibility scans found widespread color-contrast violations, which may reduce readability of counts, validation, and status text." (Severity: minor).
claims.rationale: Generic axe color-contrast findings with no named element or SPEC-covered behavior; the SPEC sets no contrast requirement, so this is polish, not a defect claim that can be credited.

claims.text: Widespread color-contrast accessibility violations. Evidence: "Widespread accessibility color-contrast violations" (Severity: minor). Restates the contrast findings covered by C008.
claims.rationale: duplicate of C008

claims.text: Recorded actions are skipped when the current page snapshot drifts from the recorded baseline, so steps do not replay. Evidence: "Recorded actions are skipped when the page snapshot drifts from baseline" (Severity: minor).
claims.rationale: Recorded-action replay skipping on baseline snapshot drift describes the test harness's own replay mechanics, not any behavior of the product.

claims.text: On the decline flow, the confirmation control sits below the reason field and is hidden from view. Evidence: "Decline confirmation control is hidden below the reason field" (Severity: major).
claims.rationale: The Confirm decline control exists and works (the decline completed elsewhere in the run); sitting below the reason field/fold is layout preference, not a SPEC violation. Distinct from f-decline-status-line, which is about the missing running status line.

claims.text: A weekday pickup date outside the allowed range is not rejected with a range message; the form instead keeps showing the stale weekend error. Evidence: after setting the date to "2026-04-15, which is a weekday but outside the displayed allowed range of 2026-03-16 to 2026-03-30" and clicking Continue to review, "The form remains on Step 2 with pickup date 2026-04-15, but still displays \"The desk is closed at weekends. Choose a weekday.\" even though that date is not a weekend."
claims.rationale: Verified via curl that the clean server returns the correct 'Pickup date must be on or before 2026-03-30.' for 2026-04-15, so the stale weekend message is a client-side validation gap. No catalog fault touches pickup-date validation, so the behavior is shared with the clean build and violates SPEC 7.2's ordered date checks and 1.6's message conventions.

claims.text: Invalid pickup dates (Saturday and out-of-window) produced no immediate date-specific validation; the date problem stayed unsurfaced while the invalid Units field blocked continuing. Evidence: "The Saturday and out-of-window pickup dates showed no immediate date-specific validation; attempts to continue were blocked by the still-invalid Units field, leaving the date probl[em unsurfaced]" (Severity: minor). Restates the broken pickup-date validation feedback covered by C012.
claims.rationale: duplicate of C012

claims.text: Confirming cancellation of ready-for-pickup loan L-1043 has no effect: the loan is never withdrawn. Evidence: after clicking "Cancel loan" then "Yes, cancel loan", "The page remains on \"Loan L-1043 Ready for pickup\". The confirmation prompt stays visible, the status is unchanged, and the loan is not withdrawn." Expected the loan to change to Cancelled/withdrawn and its "2 GoPro units" returned to stock.
claims.rationale: Exactly the catalog manifestation: 'Yes, cancel loan' on L-1043 does nothing, status stays Ready for pickup. Verified the clean reference cancels L-1043 correctly ('L-1043 cancelled. 2 units are back in stock.').

claims.text: Cancellation of a ready-for-pickup loan does not complete. Evidence: "Ready-for-pickup loan cancellation does not complete" (Severity: major). Restates the non-functional loan cancellation covered by C014.
claims.rationale: duplicate of C014

claims.text: With the cancellation confirmation failing, no alternate visible path exists to withdraw the booking, so the stock-return workflow cannot be completed from the loan record. Evidence: "There was no alternate visible path to withdraw the booking once the confirmation action failed, so the user could not complete the required stock-return workflow from the loan rec[ord]" (Severity: major). This is the same user-observable defect as C014: the loan cannot be withdrawn.
claims.rationale: duplicate of C014

claims.text: After the initial booking confirmation, the loan was not actually confirmed but was routed to supervisor approval; the reporter notes the app explained the approval reasons and provided a path forward. Evidence: "After the initial booking confirmation, the loan was not actually confirmed; it was sent for supervisor approval. The app did explain the approval reasons and provided a path to ap[prove]" (Severity: minor). May be expected behavior rather than a defect; recorded for classification.
claims.rationale: Routing a qualifying booking to supervisor approval with the reasons shown is exactly SPEC R5/7.3 behavior; the reporter even notes the app explained the reasons and the path forward.

claims.text: The L-1045 decline reason control was unstable: the same baseline locator matched 2 then 3 elements, and the entered reason appeared to be lost or reset, forcing re-entry. Evidence: "the same baseline locator was ambiguous with 2 then 3 matches, and the entered reason appeared to be lost or reset, forcing the u[ser]" (Severity: major).
claims.rationale: Ambiguous baseline locators matching 2 then 3 elements is automated-driver instability; the reported reason loss is framed as a consequence of re-driving the control, not a demonstrated product defect.

claims.text: Charges for a declined loan remain included in the "Charges booked today" figure. Evidence: "Declined loan charges remain included in Charges booked today" (Category: data_mismatch, Severity: major).
claims.rationale: Verified on the clean reference: the $341.00 tile is L-1044 only; declining L-1045 (booked 13 Mar, never counted per R6) correctly leaves it at $341.00, and declining L-1044 correctly drops it to $0.00. The declined loan's charges were never included, so the claim's premise is wrong.

claims.text: The "Charges booked today" figure is ambiguous or potentially stale after a loan decline. Evidence: "Charges booked today is ambiguous or potentially stale after a loan decline." (Category: data_mismatch, Severity: minor). Restates the declined-charges accounting issue covered by C019.
claims.rationale: duplicate of C019

claims.text: On the overdue return page, the primary return controls and note field require scrolling twice to reach, adding friction to the desk check-in workflow (the check-in itself succeeded). Evidence: "the user had to scroll twice to reach the return controls and note field. For a desk workflow on an overdue return page, the primary [controls should be visible]" (Severity: minor).
claims.rationale: Check-in succeeded; having to scroll to the return controls is layout friction, not a SPEC violation.

claims.text: The equipment picker cannot reliably select the MacBook Pro 16-inch Edit Laptop by its label. Evidence: "Equipment picker cannot reliably select MacBook Pro 16-inch Edit Laptop by label" (Severity: minor).
claims.rationale: Selecting an option 'by label' is a driver operation; the MacBook Pro 16" name contains a quote character that trips locators. No product misbehavior is described, only the automated picker's reliability.

claims.text: The loan detail page requires repeated vertical scrolling to reconcile the schedule, charge breakdown, and supervisor approval reason during a readback task. Evidence: "The loan detail page requires repeated vertical scrolling to reconcile schedule details with the charge breakdown and supervisor approval reason, adding friction to a readback task" (Severity: minor).
claims.rationale: Scrolling to reconcile panels on the loan detail page is reading friction; the SPEC prescribes these panels and no viewport requirement.

claims.text: On the approvals page, L-1045's action controls are below the fold beneath L-1044, forcing a scroll before the target loan can be declined. Evidence: "L-1045's action controls were below the fold beneath L-1044, so the user had to scroll before they could decline the target loan." (Severity: minor).
claims.rationale: SPEC 8 orders approval cards by loan number ascending, so L-1045 sits beneath L-1044; needing to scroll to it is layout preference, not a violation.

claims.text: L-1045's action controls on the approvals page were below the fold, requiring scrolling to reach them. Evidence: "L-1045's action controls were below the fold" (Severity: minor). Restates the approvals-page below-the-fold placement covered by C024.
claims.rationale: duplicate of C024

claims.text: The final Confirm decline button sat below the visible textarea after the reason was entered, requiring scrolling to reach it. Evidence: "the final Confirm decline button was below the visible textarea after entering th[e reason]" (Severity: minor). Restates the hidden decline confirmation control covered by C011.
claims.rationale: duplicate of C011

claims.text: After adding the Canon C70, the Add equipment picker resets to Aputure while the Canon row remains below, creating a possible mismatch between the picker's selected value and the already-added item. Evidence: "The Add equipment picker resets to Aputure after adding Canon C70 while the Canon row remains below, creating a possible mismatch between the selected equipment control and the alr[eady added item]" (Severity: minor).
claims.rationale: SPEC 7.2 removes already-added items from the Add equipment list, so the select naturally shows the first remaining item (Aputure, alphabetically first) while the Canon row stays in the table; the 'possible mismatch' is speculative, not an observed defect.

claims.text: The equipment picker resets after adding the Canon C70. Evidence: "Equipment picker resets after adding Canon C70" (Severity: minor). Restates the picker-reset behavior covered by C027.
claims.rationale: duplicate of C027

claims.text: The Available-only filter checkbox does not toggle when activated. Evidence: "Available-only filter checkbox does not toggle" (Category: no_effect, Severity: minor).
claims.rationale: Same surface and kind of wrongness as the catalog fault: activating the Available now only filter has no effect (category no_effect). Verified the clean reference filters correctly (availableOnly=1 lists 11 items, excluding the fully booked gimbal). Medium because 'does not toggle' loosely describes the checkbox rather than the ignored filtering.

claims.text: Loan L-1048 can be extended a second time despite the stated one-extension limit. Evidence: after the first extension the page "still shows an enabled \"Extend by 7 days\" button"; on the second click, "The second click succeeds. The status says \"Extended. L-1048 is now due Thu 2 Apr 2026 at 17:00\" and the schedule shows Due back Thu 2 Apr 2026 while still saying \"One 7-day extension used\"."
claims.rationale: Exactly the catalog manifestation: after one extension L-1048 still offers an enabled Extend button and a second extension succeeds, moving the due date to Thu 2 Apr 2026. Verified the clean reference refuses the second extension with 'This loan has already used its one extension.'

claims.text: On the borrower step, the submit action is placed below the initial viewport and is not visible without scrolling. Evidence: "Borrower step submit action is below the initial viewport" (Severity: minor).
claims.rationale: The borrower-step submit button being below the initial viewport is layout preference; the SPEC specifies the buttons but no fold placement.
